title: Using the toolbox
description:
Use `collections`, `itertools` and `functools` from lesson 5.04:

```python
def top_letters(text, n): ...            # the n most common letters (a-z, ignoring case) as (letter, count); ties alphabetical
def by_extension(filenames): ...         # dict extension -> sorted names; files without a dot go under ""; extensions lower-case
def moving_average(values, window): ...  # list of the averages of each full window of consecutive values
def staircases(n): ...                   # ways to climb n steps taking 1 or 2 at a time; fast for n = 200 (use lru_cache)
```

`moving_average([1, 2, 3, 4], 2)` is `[1.5, 2.5, 3.5]`; a window larger than the list gives `[]`. Use a `deque(maxlen=window)`. The extension is the part after the **last** dot.
hints: `Counter.items()` gives (letter, count) pairs; sort them with the key `(-count, letter)`.
Without `@lru_cache`, `staircases(200)` would take longer than the universe has existed; with it, each n is computed once.
